title: arrays and dynamic arrays for algorithmic problem solving
concepts: An array stores an ordered sequence accessed by integer index
Direct indexed access and scanning have different costs from insertion and deletion in the middle
A dynamic array combines contiguous storage with a separate logical count and allocated capacity
Resizing copies elements and makes append constant-time amortized rather than worst-case constant-time
In-place algorithms trade extra storage for mutation and careful index management
Rectangular and jagged arrays represent different multidimensional shapes
Choose arrays and dynamic arrays when order, indexed access, or compact sequential storage fit the task

practiceProblems.name: Two Sum
practiceProblems.statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Assume exactly one solution exists and do not use the same element twice. Return the indices in any order.

practiceProblems.name: Contains Duplicate
practiceProblems.statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.

practiceProblems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
practiceProblems.statement: Given an integer array prices where prices[i] is the stock price on day i, choose one day to buy and a different later day to sell. Return the maximum profit; return 0 if no profitable transaction is possible.
constraints: The buy day must be strictly earlier than the sell day.

practiceProblems.name: Rotate Array
practiceProblems.statement: Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative. Perform the operation in-place.
